newsitem.title: UK: UK government restores union rights at GCHQ.
newsitem.headline: UK government restores union rights at GCHQ.

text.p: The government announced on Thursday that it was restoring the rights of employees at the Government Communications Headquarters (GCHQ) to join a trade union.
"The conditions of service at GCHQ have been changed: they once again have the freedom they previously enjoyed to join any trade union they choose," Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said in a statement.
In 1984, the then Conservative government announced that workers at GCHQ, the listening post for Britain's intelligence services, could in future only be represented by a staff council.
The ban on trade unions, which the Conservatives said was necessary to protect national security, became a cause celebre for the Labour Party and its trade union allies.

Cook said there will now be talks with unions to "secure a collective agreement on no disruption to the work of GCHQ which will ensure that GCHQ's operations are protected from any threat of industrial action".
He said former employees at the Cheltenham, western England, agency who were sacked for continuing their union membership will now be free to apply for re-employment if they are still of working age.
"Each case will be treated sympathetically, within the normal Civil Service rules for such employment," he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
